page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Michaelis constant defined
steps.margin_note: Three lines. The two quantities are different: concentration, and rate.
lines: The Michaelis constant (Km) is the SUBSTRATE
CONCENTRATION at which the reaction rate is
steps.why: Km is a concentration read off the point where the rate is half its maximum, so both halves of the sentence have to name different quantities.
common_mistakes: Saying Km is half the maximum rate. Km is a CONCENTRATION, read at half the maximum rate.
Leaving out the word 'half'. It is what fixes the point on the curve.
steps.memory_tip: Km is a concentration, measured at half the top speed.

steps.label: What it measures
steps.margin_note: One line on what a low Km means. This half is the mark most answers skip.

lines.text: Low Km means the enzyme grips its substrate

A LOW Km means only a little substrate is

steps.why: A small Km means the enzyme reaches half speed at a low concentration, which only happens if it binds the substrate readily.
common_mistakes: Saying a high Km means strong binding. It is the opposite: LOW Km means strong binding.
Giving only the definition. The second mark is for what the number tells you.
steps.memory_tip: Less substrate needed means a tighter hold.
